title: I Hear You: Does Quality Improve with Customer Voice?
eligible_reason: Binary absorbing treatment (after_responding) switching on at hotel-specific first-response months: 3,110 treated hotels over 105 distinct monthly cohorts (first_response_ymfe 4..112), 3,062 of them with both pre and post reviews, plus 1,070 never-treated hotels. Table 6 and Table 9 are static TWFE (hotel + year-month FE, no controls, cluster hotel) on review-level data assigned to stable hotel units; Table 5/Figure 3 and Table 8/Figure 4 report Callaway-Sant'Anna (did::att_gt, not-yet-treated controls, no covariates) on the hotel-month panel.
design_notes: Package: readme.txt, stata_replication_code.do (Tables 1,2,4,6,7,9-12,14-31, Figure 5), r_replication_code.R (Figures 1-5, Tables 5 and 8 via did::att_gt). Data: rating_data.dta (1,855,527 Expedia reviews, 4,180 hotels, 50 cities, 2004-2013, 112 year-months) and hotel_senti_rating_price.dta (anonymized, for price-control robustness). Outcome exp_stars at review level; sentiment outcomes senti_score_0..4 for a subset. Treated = ever responded on TripAdvisor. CSA specs collapse to hotel x month means (rating = round(mean(exp_stars),2)). All other tables add lagged cumulative rating/review controls (ineligible) or interactions. No weights. Note the 'interval' variable (30-day intervals around first response) is used for window-restricted robustness (Table 20).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Computed from rating_data.dta: 105 distinct first_response_ymfe values among 3,110 treated hotels (94 among the 1,252 low-rated treated hotels). 112 calendar months in the panel.

specs.sample_condition: all reviews (N=1,855,527 rows; 4,180 hotels)
specs.treatment_definition: after_responding = 1 for Expedia reviews of hotel h posted on/after the date of the hotel's first management response on TripAdvisor (hotel-specific first_response_ymfe); 0 before and for never-responding hotels (treated==0).
